title: Prefill/Decode Safety Thermostat + Metaheuristic Path Planner
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: We need a conservative, production-safe mechanism that chooses execution primitives (operator/kernel variants and routing decisions) per-request for mixed prefill/decode conversational workloads. The mechanism should (1) bias toward low-variance, SLA-friendly options when tail-latency risk is high, (2) allow occasional exploration of higher-throughput kernels to reduce cost when safe, and (3) respect architecture (GPU topology, chiplet/SM fragmentation) and sequence-length fingerprints.

Motivation: Recent production incidents show that aggressive kernel switching to maximize throughput causes sporadic tail latency regressions on mixed conversational traffic. Pure bandit/greedy autotuners reduce average cost but expose the tail. We need a hybrid strategy that intentionally trades a small amount of throughput for tail stability while still adapting to workload changes.

Proposed approach: Implement a two-tier runtime advisor: (A) a lightweight "Thermostat" safety controller that monitors short-window latency/variance, occupancy, and KV cache hit behavior and enforces conservative constraints (e.g., disable high-burst kernels when tail risk exceeds threshold); (B) a metaheuristic path planner that runs a constrained, low-cost simulated-annealing style search at request-aggregation boundaries to propose kernel mixes for short horizons (10s-60s), using an ensemble cost function: weighted(RegulatedLatency, ExpectedTokensCost, VariancePenalty, ArchitectureMismatchPenalty). The planner operates on compact fingerprints (arch tag, seqlen bucket, priming length, burstiness score) to pick a prioritized ordered list of execution candidates.

Key trade-offs and constraints: 
- Must keep per-request decision overhead <0.2 ms on fast-path hot code.
- Any exploratory trial must be reversible with a fast rollback and incremental telemetry.
- Do not require heavy offline training or large stateful models; algorithm should be heuristics + lightweight scoring.
- Respect per-tenant SLAs and Dedicated capacity settings: tenants with strict latency SLOs get stricter thermostat thresholds.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end evaluation on mixed conversational replay shows 95th latency reduction >= 20% vs current greedy autotuner for same P50 cost within <= 5% increase.
- No customer-visible errors introduced by planner during a 2-week canary at 1% traffic.
- Telemetry surface (Console) exposes planner decisions, candidate scores, and rollback events.

Deliverables: 
1) Runtime advisor library (C++/Rust) integrated into the runtime decision point.
2) Lightweight in-memory fingerprint cache and recent-window telemetry aggregator.
3) Simulated-annealing metaheuristic module with configuration knobs exposed via feature flags.
4) Dashboard widgets and logging schema for rollouts and regression detection.

Notes on evaluation: Use replayed traffic from conv-burst-2026 Q1 dataset (synth + production-sampled) with multi-arch targets (A100, H100, L40). Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, cost-per-1000-tokens, variance, rollback rate.
acceptance_criteria: 95th latency reduced by >= 20% compared to baseline greedy autotuner (on mixed conversational replay)
P50 cost within +5% of baseline when 95th improvement achieved
No increase in 5xx or error-rate in canary (1% traffic) over 2 weeks
Planner decisions and rollback events appear in Console with correct attribution labels
technical_notes: Thermostat: configurable short-window (30s) sliding percentile monitor with hysteresis to avoid flapping
Metaheuristic budget: max 50 candidate score evaluations per aggregation window, limit wall time to 5 ms total per window

Score function components: latency_score (from lightweight microbench lookup), cost_score (token-weighted), variance_penalty (recent stddev multiplier), arch_mismatch_penalty (binary), tenancy_penalty (tenant SLA override)
Exploration rules: only allow candidate trials when thermostat indicates tail risk below safety threshold; trials run as shadow or on low-priority capacity where supported
Fallbacks: maintain deterministic fallback list ordered by latency-safety; ensure atomic switch and immediate rollback on telemetry spike
rollout_plan: Dev integration: feature-branch runtime + unit tests (2d)
Stage tests: replay on staging cluster with synthetic bursts (3d)
Performance bench: microbench heatmap across A100/H100/L40 (2d)
Canary: 1% traffic (2 weeks) with automated rollback if P95 latency regresses > 5%
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over multiple cycles if stable

2026-03-06 - Priya Nair (SRE): Suggested adding occupancy-aware gating to avoid chiplet stranding during burst waves. Added runbook item to monitor occupancy-deficit metric.
2026-03-08 - Design review with Console team: Agreed to add planner decision trace lines to per-route timeline widget. UX asked for compact summary (top-3 candidates) rather than full score dump.

2026-03-09 - Liam Patel: Metaheuristic module prototype complete. Simulated-annealing style scorer picks stable candidate set on replay runs; initial bench shows P95 down 18% but cost up 3%. Need further tuning of variance_penalty weight.

2026-03-10 - PM sync (Ana Romero): Decided to prioritize safety: tighten thermostat thresholds for enterprise tenants and add explicit opt-out flag for Dedicated reserved pools. Targeting canary start 2026-03-15.
